All models for the CICERO $NLG$ generative tasks were trained with the Adafactor optimizer (Shazeer and Stern, 2018) with a learning rate of 5e-6. The models CICERO $MCQ$ alternative selection were trained with the AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter,

2018) optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-5. We used a batch size of 4 for all our experiments.

The T5 Large and GLUCOSE-T5 Large have 770M parameters each. The RoBERTa-Large and ELECTRA-Large have 355M and 335M parameters, respectively. We also use a BART-Large and COMET-Large models for more extensive experiments (Appendix B). Both the models have 406M parameters. We use a single RTX 8000 GPU for our experiments. All models were trained for 5 epochs. Training and inference for the generative tasks i.e., $\mathsf{CICERO}_{NLG}$ require between 1.5-6 hours in this GPU. Training and inference for the alternative selection task i.e., $\mathsf{CICERO}_{MCQ}$ require a total of 15 hours. Training and inference times are $40\%$ less for zero-shot setting experiments.
